tx.t: Today I want to explain why sleep is so important, and what happens in the brain during the night. Adults need between seven and nine hours of sleep a night, while teenagers need eight to ten.

A full cycle of sleep lasts about ninety minutes, and we go through four or five cycles each night. Most vivid dreams happen during a stage called REM sleep, when the eyes move quickly under the eyelids.

While we sleep, the brain moves memories from short-term storage into long-term storage. Lack of sleep makes it harder to concentrate and slows reaction times, which is why tired drivers cause many accidents.
On average, people spend about one third of their lives asleep.

tx.t: Today we look at how printing changed the world. Before printing, every book in Europe was copied by hand, usually by monks, which took months.

Around fourteen forty, a German goldsmith called Johannes Gutenberg developed a printing press with movable metal letters. William Caxton set up the first printing press in England in fourteen seventy-six.
By the year fifteen hundred, historians estimate that more than twenty million books had been printed in Europe. Cheaper books helped literacy spread and made it easier to share new scientific ideas.

tx.t: Let us begin with the early history of the bicycle. The first machine of this kind was built in eighteen seventeen by a German baron called Karl von Drais, and it had no pedals.

In the eighteen sixties, pedals were fixed to the front wheel, and the machines were nicknamed boneshakers because of their hard wheels. In the eighteen seventies, the penny-farthing had a huge front wheel, which made it fast but dangerous.

The safety bicycle of the eighteen eighties had two wheels of the same size and a chain driving the back wheel. In eighteen eighty-eight, John Dunlop introduced the air-filled tyre, which made riding far more comfortable.

tx.t: Today I would like to talk about the Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system in the world. It lies off the coast of Queensland in north-eastern Australia.
It stretches for roughly two thousand three hundred kilometres. It is not one reef but a network of nearly three thousand individual reefs.
More than one thousand five hundred species of fish live there, together with many kinds of turtles and sharks. It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in nineteen eighty-one.
Scientists say that rising sea temperatures are the greatest long-term threat to the reef.

tx.t: Today I would like to describe a bike-sharing scheme in the town of Harwood. It began in twenty eleven with three hundred and thirty-one bikes, placed at stations around the centre.
Use grew quickly. Within three years the number of journeys had risen by thirty-two per cent, and on a busy day there were more than twenty-eight thousand trips.
The scheme soon met a serious problem: bikes being left in the wrong places. The council solved it with marked parking zones with a small fine for leaving a bike outside them.
Today, a ride costs two pounds sixty for the first half hour, and the first fifteen minutes are free for residents.
